Alex: Quick heads-up — when I flip FP8 (transformer-engine fused kernels) to enabled on h100 in staging, we see a recurring tail latency spike for long sequences (>1024) after ~300 requests. Anyone else hitting this?
Priya: Saw a similar pattern on L40S last week, but only when KV cache hit-rate was low. Warmup + batch coalescing seemed to make it worse.
Marco: Can you paste the runtime profile and kernel selection log? curious which FP8 kernel variant the router picks (fp8_fused vs fp8_split vs int8_fallback).
Alex: Logs + top profile: 
```
[2026-03-15 14:22:11] selected_kernel=fp8_fused_transformer_v2 occupancy=0.62
[2026-03-15 14:22:11] seq_len=2048 batch=8 kv_cache_hit=0.12
[2026-03-15 14:22:12] tail_latency p99=185ms
```
Profile top ops: 
```
gpu_time(ms)  kernel
120           fp8_fused_matmul
45            kv_rebuild
20            softmax_fp8_approx
```
Marco: interesting — `kv_rebuild` is non-trivial here. could be eviction + re-materialize churn. Jin, any ideas about batching interaction?
Jin: If the batcher coalesces variable-length requests mid-warmup, kernel selector sometimes flips from `fp8_fused` -> `fp8_split`. That increases mem copies and causes a transient occupancy drop. I saw ~47 kernel switches in 30s on a similar trace.
Priya: Also common culprit: subnormal/denormal accumulation on some transformer engine paths. On L40S we fixed similar behavior by enabling accumulator-in-fp32 and clamping subnormals. Try transformer_engine configs: `accumulate_in_fp32=true`, `clamp_subnormals=true`.
Alex: Added the transformer_engine tweak and repro logs: 
```
calib: layer.attn.q_scale 0.03125 -> 0.0625
calib: layer.mlp.w_scale 0.015625 -> 0.015625
runtime: kv_eviction triggered kv_resident=0.85 memory_pressure=0.78 cause=batcher_coalesce
router: kernel_switch_count=47
```
Priya: That calibration change (q_scale doubled) is worrying — might be losing dynamic range and pushing values into saturation for the softmax approximation. Could lead to extra compute in the approximation shim.
Marco: Hypothesis: calibration pushed some layers into a scale regime where `softmax_fp8_approx` loses accuracy and runtime inserts corrective passes, hurting latency. We should compare outputs vs fp32 on a validation set.
Jin: Short-term workaround: force kernel policy for long sequences to `int8_fallback` or `fp32_stable` in canary. In `/etc/redwood/runtime/policies` I used `route.policy.long_seq_kernel=int8_fallback` — removed the spikes locally.
perf-bot: Perf alert: regression detected on staging for h100-fp8 canary (commit abc123) — p99 increased by +120ms. https://ci.internal/perf/abc123
Alex: I tried Jin's fallback — spikes disappear but token cost +12%. Tradeoff looks acceptable for now while we root cause.
Priya: Action items: 1) re-run calibration with per-channel hist bins and cap max_scale, 2) add `kernel_switch_rate` and `kv_warmup_hit` metrics to runtime, 3) patch batcher to prefer stable kernel if switch_rate > threshold.
Marco: I'll open PRs for the metrics and the batcher heuristic change. Also will add a perf test that simulates warmup+low-kv-hit workload (seq 1024-2048 mix).
Alex: I'll run a 24h soak with `int8_fallback` on canary and attach traces. If soak passes, we ship fallback policy and iterate on calibration.
Priya: FYI — capturing the full GPU timeline helped: nvtx ranges showed repeated small memcpy spikes coincident with kernel switches. That lines up with memory-traffic increase when selector flips.
Jin: +1 on nvtx. Also collect transformer-engine counters (kernel occupancy, warp_eff) — they show occupancy dropping from 0.92 -> 0.58 during incidents.
Alex: Thanks all — I'll post the soak results tomorrow. :thumbsup:
